metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment alternates frequently (e.g., +1/-1 cycles), model tends to over-forecast early in the cycle and under-forecast late — adjust forecast mid-cycle by reducing slope or adding mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >30% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ consecutive days, model tends to over-forecast downward — apply upward bias to counteract mean-reversion bias.
- Model underestimates true volatility during sentiment shifts — increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment if sentiment flips >2x in 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture 1–2 week mean-reversion tail — add 1–2% upward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model is underestimating bullish momentum — add 2–3% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
